projects.name: Disease burden reduced through strengthened antimicrobial resistance surveillance and stewardship, accelerated neglected tropical disease elimination efforts, and implementation of evidence-informed policies and multisectoral actions for noncommunicable disease prevention and control.
projects.description: This sub-output consolidates eight former sub-outputs: "Promoting evidence-based advocacy and implementing robust health and economic monitoring mechanisms for managing NCDs... (Strategies 3, 4 & 5)" (ID 82469); "Improve the quality and reach of essential health services" (ID 182895); "National workforce strategies strengthened and National Health Assembly resolution 2024 on transforming workforce for healthy society" (ID 207682); "Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) surveillance and stewardship enhanced" (ID 207687); "Neglected Tropical Disease elimination and treatment supported" (ID 207690); "Mental health promotion, surveillance, and digital services expanded" (ID 207691); "Healthy ageing and integrated care for older people promoted" (ID 207696); and "NCD risk factor reduction policies and enforcement mechanisms strengthened" (ID 207697). Multisectoral action on NCDs was enhanced through improved partnerships facilitated by the UN Thematic Working Group, aligned with NCD Strategies 3, 4 and 5, complementing the workforce strengthening achieved through enhanced HRH provider registries and a landscape analysis of the community non-professional workforce. Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) management was advanced through co-hosting a Multi-Country Meeting on AMR and Primary Health Care, a Point Prevalence Survey on healthcare-associated infections across 100 hospitals, and development of a national AMR burden methodology and antimicrobial stewardship tools. Progress towards elimination of Neglected Tropical Diseases was supported through provision of diagnostic test strips for Lymphatic Filariasis and sustained treatment of leprosy cases through procurement and distribution of essential medication. Mental health services were expanded through the nationwide scale-up of the "Step-by-Step" digital application, the "Tor term Jai" platform, and the WHO LIVE LIFE suicide prevention package, alongside capacity building through the 3rd International Mental Health Workforce Training. Healthy ageing was promoted through implementation of the Integrated Care for Older People (ICOPE) approach with Siriraj Hospital, alongside advocacy to address social isolation among older persons. NCD risk factor reduction was advanced through sustained advocacy for "Best Buys" policies, including health taxes, e-cigarette bans, food reformulation, Milk Code enforcement, and alcohol control policy assessment.

projects.name: Country capacity strengthened for health emergency preparedness, prevention, detection and response through enhanced health security systems, emergency operations, risk communication, community engagement, mass gathering preparedness, and implementation of the International Health Regulations (IHR).
projects.description: This sub-output consolidates five former sub-outputs: "Improving national capability to prepare, prevent, detect and respond to public health emergencies (PHE)" (ID 82366); "Regional health security and national risk assessment capacities strengthened" (ID 207683); "Emergency response operations and mass gathering preparedness supported" (ID 207684); "National health security capacities and IHR systems strengthened" (ID 207685); and "Risk communication and community-based emergency preparedness strengthened" (ID 207686). WHO supported the establishment of the Secretariat for the ASEAN Centre for Public Health Emergencies and Emerging Diseases (ACPHEED) and strengthened national surveillance by integrating the Quick and Immediate Risk Assessment (QIRA) tool into the Standard Operating Procedures of National Situation Awareness Teams. Emergency response capacity was bolstered through procurement of essential supplies for the cholera response to spillover cases from Myanmar, the provision of shelter and psychosocial support materials for the border conflict response, and support to the Ministry of Public Health for mass gathering preparedness during the SEA Games. National preparedness was further enhanced through implementation of the Hospital Safety Index across Ministry of Public Health hospitals, strengthened provincial Emergency Operations Center capacities, upgraded Event-Based and genomic Surveillance for respiratory pathogens in high-tourism locations, and establishment of the National IHR Authority. Risk communication was advanced by piloting the Information Environment Assessment to address infodemics and by strengthening linkages between the Public Health Emergency Operations Center's risk communication channels and Village and Migrant Health Volunteer networks.

projects.description:
This suboutput comprises of multiple ILO projects:
1. TRIANGLE in ASEAN (2011 - 2025)
2. TRIANGLE Partnerships (2026 - 2031)
3. Realizing Women Migrant Workers' Rights and Opportunities in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations - Safe and Fair (2018 -2023)

Focus areas for the ILO's labour migration programming include protecting and promoting of the rights of women and men migrant workers including on fair recruitment and working conditions; contributing to economic development and inclusive growth – in particular labour mobility, skills development and recognition, and increasing development impact; contributing to climate resilience; reintegration; advocacy (with UNHCR) on labour market access for refugees and forcibly displaced persons; supporting national and regional dialogues on labour migration; and improving harmonised data collection and statistics.

projects.name: Advanced resilient, evidence-informed and environmentally sustainable health systems through strengthened governance, health technology assessment, and progress towards universal health coverage, while integrating climate adaptation, air pollution control, sustainable waste management and biodiversity protection into national health policies and programmes.
projects.description: This sub-output consolidates three former sub-outputs: "Strengthen public health resilience to climate and environmental risks" (ID 182894); "Universal Health Coverage and health systems governance advanced" (ID 207700); and "Health technology assessment and economic evidence generation supported" (ID 207701). projects.name: State and non-state actors have increased knowledges and mechanisms to advance and localize gender equality and women empowerment to integrate/mainstream gender responsiveness at national and local level to promote women peace and cybersecurity and digital literacy.
projects.description:
In 2023, following the advice of UN Women, the agency combined two sub-outputs and modified the sub-output statement accordingly. The original sub-output (SOU 7) aimed to enhance the knowledge and mechanisms of state and non-state actors to promote gender equality and integrate gender responsiveness at the national and local levels. The allocated resources for 2022 were $60,000, but only $20,000 was available, and the expenditure was $56,426. To address this inconsistency, the available resource amount was adjusted to $56,426.

The second sub-output (SOU 11) focused on the Royal Thai Government (RTG) acquiring knowledge on gender-responsive approaches to prioritize gender equality and women's empowerment in budgeting and procurement at the local and national levels. The allocated resources for 2022 were $10,000, with $5,000 available and $2,000 expended.

Now, these two sub-outputs have been integrated into a revised sub-output (Revised SOU 7). The revised statement emphasizes that state and non-state actors have increased their knowledge and mechanisms to advance gender equality and integrate gender responsiveness at the national and local levels. Additionally, it includes a specific focus on gender-responsive budgeting as a means to promote the prioritization of gender equality and women's empowerment.


The original sub-output statement (SOU 7): State and non-state actors have increased knowledges and mechanisms to advance and localize gender equality and women's empowerment  and to integrate/mainstream gender-responsive approach in their policy or operational framework at national and local level
The original sub-output statement (SOU 11): The Royal Thai Government (RTG) gain the knowledge on gender-responsive approach to advance gender responsive budgeting/procurement at local and national level to ensure that gender equality and women's empowerment are prioritized.

The integrated sub-output is now (Revised SOU 7): "State and non-state actors have increased knowledges and mechanisms to advance and localize gender equality and to integrate/mainstream gender responsiveness at national and local level including gender-responsive budgeting to promote prioritization of gender equality and women empowerment. "

Tuberculosis control was advanced through the 1st National TB Conference, a comprehensive review of Thailand's TB epidemiological data, and piloting of AI-powered computer-aided detection for TB and early cancer detection in resource-limited settings. Malaria elimination efforts targeting Vivax malaria were advanced through the funding and introduction of a 7-day Primaquine and Tafenoquine treatment protocol, complemented by novel G-6PD deficiency testing to ensure safe treatment administration. NCD management and monitoring were strengthened by documenting best practices under the Diabetes Remission Initiative, developing a draft health-economics Monitoring and Evaluation framework, and implementing the WHO SEAHEARTS technical package in Lampang and Chiang Mai to improve hypertension management in primary health care. Immunization coverage was enhanced through the Vaccine Avengers Programme, which boosted measles-rubella coverage in low-performing provinces, alongside strengthened community outreach, real-time tracking dashboards, Adverse Events Following Immunization (AEFI) surveillance, and continued support for Measles and Rubella elimination and Polio-free status by 2026.

projects.name: By the end of 2026, Thailand will have fully integrated Inclusive Green Economy principles into the national development plan and BCG model by implementing evidence-based sectoral reforms (PAGE)
projects.description: The Partnership for Action on Green Economy (PAGE) is a collaborative initiative among five UN Agencies (UNEP, UNDP, UNIDO, UNITAR, and ILO) to support countries in transforming their economies towards green and inclusive models, aligned with the 2030 SDG Agenda and the Paris Agreement on Climate Change. In Thailand, PAGE is led by UNIDO and the National Economic and Social Development Council (NESDC).Key Achievements:1) Greening National Policies and Strategies:Green Economy Policy Scoping Report: Highlights the reforms needed for decarbonization, promoting the Bio-Circular-Green (BCG) model, renewable energy, green finance, digitalization, and capacity development.Green and Inclusive Economic Recovery Policy Assessment Report: Recommends integrating SDGs, Nationally Determined Contributions, and BCG Economic Policy into government projects and budgeting. Developed training modules focused on green and inclusive development, measuring progress with green indicators, and principles of green industry and jobs. 2) Carbon Cap and Trade for a Decarbonized Economy:Macroeconomic Planning for Green and Climate Policy Options Report and Training: Strengthens government capacity to make informed economic policy decisions, assessing socio-economic impacts of carbon tax, energy efficiency, renewable energy investments, and bio-circular-green economy investments.Emission Trading Scheme Development: Promotes national-level carbon market development, analyzing carbon pricing mechanisms and socio-economic impacts. Workshops and workplans were developed for implementing ETS in Thailand, covering all aspects from regulation to capacity building. 3) Digitalization of Financing Mechanism for Sustainable Waste Management:Based on assessments and collaborations with the Department of Local Administration, mobile applications are being developed to enhance local government capacities in managing waste cycles sustainably.
projects.outcome: Green growth: An inclusive and sustainable economic growth premised on Thailand’s bio-circular-green model is supported.

projects.name: Strengthening the capacity of women human rights defenders,  survivors of human rights violations, and their families to improve access to justice.
projects.description:
Note on Unspent Budget – OHCHR WHRD Project
Reported by: Dip Mager, OHCHR
Date: 9 April 2025, 23:09
The OHCHR Women Human Rights Defenders (WHRD) project/activity was suspended pending the review of Thailand by the CEDAW Committee. The project, funded by Sweden, was designed to support WHRD women survivors of human rights violations and their families’ engagement with the CEDAW review process. As the review did not take place in 2023 or 2024 as anticipated, the activity could not proceed and the allocated budget remained unspent.

children.name: Human capital needed for social and inclusive development is improved through strengthening of institutions, partnerships and the empowerment of people.
children.description:
The second strategic outcome for consideration contributes to the NESDP priorities enhancing Thailand’s human capital. The underlying premise is that people represent the true wealth of the nation. A healthy, well-educated and skilled population, evidenced through the high human development index and based on the foundation of being able to access and exercise human rights, is a good in itself. It will act as a catalyst that drives the transformation of Thailand. The enabling environment for such a transformation is also dependent on the ability of public institutions, systems and services to successfully frame and implement a coherent integrated policy framework, based on principles of equity, accountability, transparency and efficiency. To affect such a change and achieve the impact required, public services need to concentrate on measures that drive standards and outcomes upwards through a focus on quality improvement. To focus the UN’s support on the attainment of this outcome, the UN will collaborate with the Government and development partners including civil society, businesses and communities to prioritize two focus areas, which contribute to nine of the milestones prioritized in the draft 13th Plan. 
- Human capital development through enhancing access to quality of public services,
- Digital inclusion and transformation

children.name: People living in Thailand, especially those at risk of being left furthest behind, are able to participate in and benefit from development, free from all forms of discrimination.
children.description: The aspiration to leave no one behind is the touchstone of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Women and LGBTI people in particular lag behind their male counterparts across much of Thailand’s social, economic and political life. The energy and dynamism of young people will play a key role in catalysing Thailand’s enterprising culture in the post-COVID-19 landscape. Equally, older people should experience healthy and active aging, as Thailand is an ageing society. Ethnic populations and people living in rural and remote areas should have equal opportunity to those residing in urban areas. Evidence consistently shows the criminalization, stigma, discrimination and other human rights violations towards people infected and affected by HIV reduce service uptake and increase HIV infection. As already noted, the digital divide, nationality as well as status can hold populations back from benefitting and contributing towards Thailand’s collective development journey. In short, where barriers to inclusion and development exist, they need to be systematically dismantled and replaced with enabling opportunities and services.
